1.title: Modern Operations, Reliability and Resilience
1.text: Welcome to Module thirteen: Modern Operations, Reliability and Resilience. It covers the exam area six. Scaling with Google Cloud operations. Each part of this module comes from the study notes of the same name, so you can read the notes after you watch.

1.title: What You Will Learn
1.text: By the end of this module you will be able to do six things. six point two Describe the fundamental concepts of modern operations, reliability and resilience in the cloud: modernizing operations with Google Cloud Observability (operations suite, Cloud Monitoring, Cloud Logging, Cloud Trace, Cloud Profiler, Error Reporting). Operations terms (operational excellence, reliability, high availability). Designing resilient infrastructure (redundancy, replication, scalable infrastructure, backups). Measuring performance and reliability (latency, traffic, saturation, errors). dev ops and Site Reliability Engineering (S L Is, S L Os, S L As). Practice with exam-style questions and a recall check.

1.title: Where This Fits in the Exam
1.text: Here is where this module sits in the exam. Exam area: six. Scaling with Google Cloud operations (about ten percent). Exam format: ninety minutes and fifty to sixty multiple-choice questions. Validated against: the official Google Cloud Digital Leader exam guide.

1.title: Operations terms
1.text: Operations terms. Operational excellence. Running systems well: efficient, automated, continuously improved. Reliability. The system does what users expect, when they expect it. High availability (H A). Minimal downtime, often by removing single points of failure. Resilience. Withstanding and recovering from failure.

1.title: Google Cloud Observability
1.text: Google Cloud Observability. Observability means seeing what is happening inside your systems so you can fix problems fast.

1.title: Google Cloud Observability, continued
1.text: Google Cloud Observability. The figure shows this: Observability products: Monitoring, Logging, Trace, Profiler and Error Reporting.

1.title: Google Cloud Observability, continued
1.text: Google Cloud Observability. Cloud Monitoring. Metrics, dashboards and alerts about health and performance. Cloud Logging. Logs from applications and services, searchable. Cloud Trace. How long requests take as they travel through services (latency). Cloud Profiler. Which parts of the code use the most C P U and memory. Error Reporting. Collects and groups application errors. Together they form the operations suite (Google Cloud Observability). Exam tip: Metrics and alerts to Monitoring. Logs to Logging. Slow requests to Trace. Heavy code to Profiler. Crashes and exceptions to Error Reporting.

1.title: Designing resilient infrastructure
1.text: Designing resilient infrastructure. Redundancy. Extra copies of components so one failure does not stop service. Replication. Copy data across zones or regions. Scalable infrastructure. Add capacity to meet demand (autoscaling). Backups. Copies to restore after loss or mistakes. Use multiple zones for high availability and multiple regions for disaster recovery.

1.title: Measuring performance and reliability: the golden signals
1.text: Measuring performance and reliability: the golden signals. Latency. How long does a request take? Traffic. How much demand is the system handling? Saturation. How full is the system (C P U, memory, capacity)? Errors. How many requests fail?

1.title: DevOps and Site Reliability Engineering (SRE)
1.text: dev ops and Site Reliability Engineering (S R E). dev ops joins development and operations for faster, more reliable releases through automation and shared ownership. S R E (site reliability engineering) applies software engineering to operations. Service level indicator (S L I). Meaning: A measurement of service behavior. Example: Percent of requests served in under three hundred milliseconds. Service level objective (S L O). Meaning: The target for an S L I. Example: ninety-nine point nine percent of requests succeed. Service level agreement. Meaning: A contract: what the provider promises and the remedy if it fails. Example: Credits if availability falls below the promise.

1.title: DevOps and Site Reliability Engineering (SRE), continued
1.text: dev ops and Site Reliability Engineering (S R E). An error budget is how much unreliability the S L O allows; it balances speed of change and stability. Exam tip: S L I measures, S L O targets, S L A (service level agreement) promises. The S L A is the contract; the S L O is the internal goal. Exam tip: Use the S R E words precisely: an S L I is measured, an S L O is the target, an S L A is the contract. Observability tells you what is wrong; resilience keeps the service up.

1.title: Practice Question 1
1.text: Question one. A team wants dashboards and alerts about the health and performance of its services. Which product fits? The four options are on the screen. The answer is C: Cloud Monitoring, which shows metrics and alerts. Cloud Monitoring provides metrics, dashboards and alerts.

1.title: Practice Question 2
1.text: Question two. A developer wants to see which function in the code uses the most C P U. Which product fits? The four options are on the screen. The answer is D: Cloud Profiler. Cloud Profiler shows which parts of the code consume the most C P U and memory.

1.title: Practice Question 3
1.text: Question three. A company wants to find which service in a chain of calls makes requests slow. Which product fits? The four options are on the screen. The answer is D: Cloud Trace, which shows request latency. Cloud Trace shows how long requests take as they pass through services.

1.title: Practice Question 4
1.text: Question four. Which design helps an application stay available if one data center area fails? The four options are on the screen. The answer is B: Redundancy across several zones. Spreading across zones removes the single point of failure and supports high availability.

1.title: Practice Question 5
1.text: Question five. A team defines that ninety-nine point nine percent of requests must succeed each month. What is this? The four options are on the screen. The answer is B: A service level objective, a target. The target for an indicator is a service level objective.

1.title: Practice Question 6
1.text: Question six. Which of the following is a contract that promises a level of service and a remedy if it is not met? The four options are on the screen. The answer is B: An S L A, which is the service contract. A service level agreement is the contract with the promised level and remedy.

1.title: Recall Check 1
1.text: Recall check one. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question one. What are the four golden signals? Answer: Latency, traffic, saturation, errors. Question two. Which product shows logs? Answer: Cloud Logging. Question three. What does Error Reporting do? Answer: Collects and groups application errors.

1.title: Recall Check 2
1.text: Recall check two. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question four. What does S L O stand for? Answer: Service level objective. Question five. What is an error budget? Answer: How much unreliability the S L O allows. Question six. Name two resilience techniques. Answer: For example redundancy and replication.

1.title: Module Recap
1.text: Here is the recap. Observability: Monitoring (metrics, alerts), Logging, Trace (latency), Profiler (code use), Error Reporting. Resilience: redundancy, replication, scalability, backups; zones for H A, regions for D R. Golden signals: latency, traffic, saturation, errors. S R E: S L I measures, S L O targets, S L A promises; error budget.
